A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabMGP research, with matching authors, core construction, experiments and Appendices A–H. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support comparison across the revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across 11 synthetic and 19 real-data setups, together with posterior coverage, runtime, convergence and concentration results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports revised baseline results and an expanded validity diagnostic.

M1.justification: The bootstrap-feature, TabPFN-response and loss-minimization construction remains. However, v2 Algorithm 1 conditions TabPFN on the original z1:n, whereas v1's predictive rule uses the growing context. V2 Figure 1 and accompanying prose still specify growing-context prediction. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a notation error or an inference change.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 30 evaluation setups, covering linear, binary logistic and multinomial logistic regression, plus the same concentration and fixed-covariate diagnostic scenarios. The additional diagnostic probes change sample coverage within an existing scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add the standalone Asymptotic comparator alongside BB, Copula and Bayes. Appendix H retains its previous comparator membership, and Copula remains omitted for multinomial regression.

E3.justification: Bayes changes from an isotropic Gaussian prior with variance 100 to the data-derived Gaussian N(theta_hat_n, H_hat_n^-1). Appendix H replaces Winkler scores with median interval widths and selects winners by coverage followed by width. The validity diagnostic also expands from eight to ten covariate probes. These materially revise the comparison protocol.

E4.justification: The a.c.i.d. diagnostic is revised from eight probes in v1 Figure 3 to ten in v2 Figure 5, with changed cumulative-drift values. The concentration experiment and individual convergence traces are retained; moving concentration into the main text does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both report 100 data repetitions, 100 MGP posterior samples and four NUTS chains totaling 8000 samples. No new seed reporting, uncertainty estimates for experimental summaries or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace Bayes results under its changed prior and add Asymptotic results. For Logistic, Bayes coverage/size changes from 0.99/1.94 to 0.53/0.78; Asymptotic reports 0.96/1.53. Appendix H replaces Winkler results with widths and revised rankings, adds the omitted t5/x2 row, and changes TabMGP's GMM(-1)/x7 coverage from 0.85 to 0.86. Main MGP results otherwise match apart from rounding.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces explicit definitions of the empirical Hessian and Gaussian approximation used for Asymptotic and the revised Bayes prior; Appendix H removes the Winkler-score definition. The core MGP definitions, a.c.i.d. conditions, PFN training derivation and Bayesian-posterior recovery argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central TabMGP construction and near-nominal-coverage claims remain. V2 narrows the conclusion from TabPFN failing both sufficient conditions to finite-horizon diagnostics not certifying them. It also removes the concluding proposal to interpret transformers through a hidden prior–likelihood pair.

C2.justification: V2 introduces numerical precision as an alternative explanation for apparent a.c.i.d. failure and substantially expands the interpretation of empirical validity diagnostics. Comparator performance is newly discussed through asymptotic accuracy and misspecification. V1's architectural limitations discussion is removed, including the warning about binning distorting uncertainty and the proposed autoregressive-training improvement.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents uniform two-dimensional feature generation, random probe selection, the grid 100,120,...,1100 and trapezoidal accumulation. Appendix E.1 specifies the Hessian-based Gaussian calculation. Existing code and checkpoint access, TabPFN version, temperature, ensembles and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Fortini et al. (2026), contrasting predictive-CLT inference with inference for loss-defined functionals. References to Berti et al. (2021) and Winkler (1972) disappear. The broader related-work survey remains; Battiston and Cappello's changed title identifies the same arXiv work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around scientific estimands and the relationship between Bayesian predictive inference and generalized Bayes. Method explanations are reorganized, validity becomes Section 3.2, and an appendix contents list is added.

P2.justification: V2 adds a sampling schematic, moves the concentration figure into the main text, redraws the validity diagnostic, and revises plot colors, legends and reference lines. Result tables are extensively reformatted into separate Rate and Size columns, with relocated captions, reordered parameter rows and revised highlighting.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, adds an analytic comparator and qualifies v1's categorical validity claim. However, its Bayes prior now uses the same data-derived approximation before updating on those observations, without discussing the implications for comparison. Algorithm 1 introduces an unresolved conditioning inconsistency, and architectural caveats are removed. These benefits and harms leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
